metadata.method_name: post-training collapse screen: 2x2 weights-by-format decomposition + sharpening-direction steering + hash-committed base-model forecast
metadata.description: Qwen3-8B-Base vs Qwen3-8B (thinking off) on two path-search tasks (T1 unweighted grid path, T2 weighted shortest path). Arms: base template-free, base chat-templated, instruct chat, instruct template-free (2x2), modal-ban arms, and HF steering arms that subtract the paired instruct-minus-base residual difference (band-incremental over layers 8-28, plus fallbacks). Every program is scored on >=44 hidden tests and labelled by a runtime-signature + AST labeller with a blind LLM judge for disagreements.

selection.rule: stratified by (pass, final label) / (fail, error kind) per arm, round-robin over paraphrases; each parseable candidate re-scored + runtime-labelled with the artifact code and kept only if it reproduced within the time cap

hidden_tests.limits_rule: limit_s = max(1.0, 10 x median-of-5 time of primary reference); calibrated on this pod

spec.t1: Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal). grid is a list of equal-length strings in which . is a free cell and # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of free cells. A move goes up, down, left or right to a free cell inside the grid. Return a list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal, including both ends; any valid path is accepted. If goal cannot be reached, return an empty list. The grid has at most 30 rows and 30 columns. Use only the Python standard library.
spec.t2: Task: write a Python function solve(n, edges, s, t). The graph is directed with nodes 0..n-1 (n <= 100). edges is a list of (u, v, w) tuples, each an edge from u to v with integer weight 0 <= w <= 100; there may be cycles, self-loops and parallel edges. Return the length of the shortest path from s to t as an int, or -1 if t is unreachable from s. If s == t return 0. Use only the Python standard library.
